title: Swim in Rising Water
keyIdea: At time t you can stand on any cell with height ≤ t, so a path can be used once t reaches its highest cell. Find the path from the top-left to the bottom-right that minimises that highest cell: Dijkstra where a path's cost is the max height on it.

approaches.name: Dijkstra on the max height
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). Min-heap of {time, r, c} starting at {grid[0][0], 0, 0}; pop the soonest cell; push unseen neighbours with max(t, height); return when the corner is popped.
approaches.why: n² cells, each pushed once into a heap of size up to n².

quiz.q: What is the cost of a path here?
Why can a cell be marked seen when it is pushed (not popped)?
options: Its key is max(t, height) and t only grows, so the first push is already the best
Because the grid is a tree
Binary search t and check with BFS/DFS if the corner is reachable
Greedy: always step to the lowest neighbour
DP from the top-left only moving right/down
